# InterestSeed — full text

Source: https://lxc248.github.io/-interestseed/
Repository: https://github.com/lxc248/-interestseed
Latest release: 4.0.7
License: AGPL-3.0-only

## What it is

InterestSeed is a local-first interest validator for any Markdown vault. It is
for people who save a lot but rarely test what they saved. It does not try to
be a read-it-later app or a general PKM workspace.

The loop is:

capture → connect → 3-day experiment → evidence → next action

## What the AI sees

The AI request is limited to:

- node ids;
- short titles;
- tags;
- existing edge id pairs.

It does not send note bodies, source paths, full vault contents, cookies or
platform data. The result is one suggestion, not a batch of pending cards.

The user decides whether to connect, skip, or change the relation. InterestSeed
does not auto-write the graph, auto-publish, or generate routes without a human
decision.

## The 3-day experiment

A connection is a hypothesis. The experiment is a small reality check, not a
clinical trial or a productivity score.

- Day 1: do one small action and write what actually happened.
- Day 2: repeat, or notice that you avoided it.
- Day 3: write the evidence, then choose continue / change / drop.

Useful evidence is concrete: what you did, for how long, what you finished,
what felt easier or harder, what you avoided, and what changed.

## Four surfaces

- CLI: scriptable scan, capture, suggest, connect and experiment commands.
- Local web: cosmic graph, one-suggestion AI panel, experiment strip and inbox.
- Agent skill: one suggestion, wait for confirmation, never auto-write.
- MCP: read-only graph context for an MCP client.

## Install

```bash
unzip interestseed-standalone-v4.0.7.zip
node interestseed-standalone-v4.0.7/cli.js init --vault "<vault>"
node interestseed-standalone-v4.0.7/cli.js serve --vault "<vault>" --port 4173
```

Open http://127.0.0.1:4173. No account, no cloud sync, no automatic graph writes.

## How it differs from Readwise

Readwise helps you collect and revisit highlights. InterestSeed tests whether a
saved interest deserves a 3-day experiment. Readwise is a capture and review
tool; InterestSeed is a decision tool. They can coexist: export highlights to
Markdown, point InterestSeed at the vault, test one connection.

## How it differs from Obsidian

Obsidian is a general local Markdown workspace. InterestSeed is a validation
layer for one job: turning a saved interest into a testable connection and a
decision. Obsidian is optional. The standalone runtime reads any Markdown
vault; the Obsidian plugin is a compatibility surface.

## FAQ

### What is InterestSeed?

InterestSeed is a local-first interest validator for any Markdown vault. Local
AI suggests one testable connection, then a 3-day experiment decides whether to
continue or drop it.

### Is InterestSeed an Obsidian plugin?

Obsidian is optional. The standalone runtime includes a CLI, a local web
dashboard, an agent skill and a read-only MCP server. The Obsidian plugin is a
compatibility surface.

### Does InterestSeed send my notes to a cloud model?

The Explore AI request sends only node ids, titles, tags and existing edge
pairs. It never sends note bodies, source paths or vault contents.

### What is a 3-day experiment?

A 3-day experiment is a small test after you connect two notes. You log one real
observation per day; evidence decides whether to continue, change the direction,
or drop the interest.

### Is InterestSeed open source?

Yes. The code is AGPL-3.0-only. The name, logo and visual identity are covered by
a separate trademark policy. Commercial closed-source or hosted use needs a
commercial license.
